I love Molly Harris. I have loved her since the first time I laid eyes on her last year. I knew right away that there was something special about Molly, something that knocked me for a loop. I was drawn to her, like a moth to light. When we first see someone stunning, someone "special," our minds shift into overtime thinking of possibilities. We build them up and put them on a pedestal, without another thought as to whether or not the inside of the book will match the outside cover. Lucky for me, Molly's inner beauty matches her outer beauty. She's a sweetheart all the way. Molly's a raven-haired English Major with dazzling green eyes. She has a younger sister named Becky and an older brother named Jeff. She's a "neglected middle child," just like me.

We didn't have any classes together, but I changed that soon enough. Sure, an American Lit class didn't exactly help me get my Chemistry degree, but we all do crazy things for love. That first class was a revelation. Molly handled wave after wave of her stern professor's questions, like a gymnast performing a gold medal routine. My Molly ran circles around the pretentious twits in her class. She wasn't like them. Sure, she knew Madame Bovary forwards and backwards just like they did, but she didn't fawn all over it like those suck-ups. She knew it was an outdated "classic" that English majors are supposed to drool over and worship, just because they're told to.

As the semester moved on, I came to know Molly intimately. We got into a routine of sorts, with her always arriving precisely five minutes after I did, a smile across her gorgeous face. Molly is a popular girl and I couldn't help but feel jealous when other boys would talk to her. We all get insecure sometimes and I'm no different. I was never that nervous about it anyway, because I knew Molly well and ours was a true love. Yes everyone says that, but this was different. Molly made my life better in every way. She helped me accept myself. She even got me into a new hobby. I find photography to be very interesting, and I've become quite skilled at it. The only other thing I've ever been nearly as good at was taxidermy, which my late father kind of forced upon me. When it came to photography, naturally my girl was my muse. She always seems so candid in her photos and her poses always bring a smile to my face.

The intimacy we share is my favorite part of our relationship. I feel like I can tell Molly anything. I treasure our private time. It's the only time I feel like I can really be myself. Unfortunately, we haven't been able to have much of it lately without being interrupted. Ever since we consummated our relationship, it seems that we can't go five minutes without someone trying to bother us. I'm not a big fan of the telephone. It always seems to ring at just the wrong moment. I don't have a cell phone, but Molly does. Sometimes I wish people would just back off and understand that we need our alone time. You wouldn't believe how many calls Molly's gotten in the past three days. It's not just one person either. Her parents, her brother, her sister, her teachers, even someone named Brad, who left some crazy panicked voicemail. He kept telling Molly he loved her and was worried about her. He also said something about coming over tonight. Some people just don't understand the meaning of privacy. Speaking of which, I've got to go now. Molly and I are having a photo shoot and I've got to get ready to help her out. After the second day, Molly just couldn't make those lifelike poses anymore without my help and I've got to get her ready for Brad's visit. I hope he enjoys my hobbies as much as I do.
